$comment: Machine-readable rules for VibeBook. Any AI assistant or script that edits this project must read this file first and follow every rule marked mustFollow. Add a rule here whenever the owner asks for a lasting convention.

rules.rule: All UI follows Android Material Design 3. Use the tokens and components in src/material.css (loaded last). Do not invent a one-off look for a screen.
Motion follows Material 3 Expressive: springy, slightly bouncy, natural. Use --spring-fast, --spring-slow and --ease-emphasized. Always honor prefers-reduced-motion.
Buttons, icon buttons, chips and tabs are rounded squares (--radius-btn, 12px). Inputs, selects, textareas and search bars use --radius-field (12px). Only avatars and dots are round.
Menus are Material 3: 48px rows, state layers (hover for mouse only, focus and press for all), no hover wash left after a tap.
Layouts must work from 280px (folded cover screen) to large tablets and unfolded foldables. Controls share width with grid/auto-fit and never overflow sideways.
Every visible change gets one short plain line in the newest release in src/changelog.ts (shown in Settings > About > What's new). Newest first.
UI text and descriptions are short and concise: one short sentence, plain words, say what the person can do. No jargon or file names in the UI.
When a feature people will notice is added, add a step for it to src/tourSteps.ts and bump TOUR_VERSION so returning users see it. The tour always has a Skip button.

Exported OJT documents must match the school's original documents (Times New Roman, tight spacing, header lines in the body, same wording and table layout). Aim for at least 80% visual match. The source documents are the reference.
Evaluation forms are filled in by the supervisor from a link. The answers are never sent to or stored in the database and the intern never sees them.
Per-device preferences (quick reaction, suggestion clearing, reminders) live in src/preferences.ts and are never stored on the server.
Bulk or irreversible actions (delete all, archive all, reset timer) need a ConfirmDialog with typeToConfirm.
Any new collection, field or notification type needs a change in firestore.rules, and the release note must say the rules need deploying.
Run `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm run build` before handing the project back.
